title: Shillong Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Shillong hotel or restaurant converts rooms, kitchen and banquet space into daily cash, and the cash arrives fast while the costs sit fixed.** Rooms and F&B revenue is collected at checkout or on the event date, so the working-capital cycle is short and favourable; the real risk sits in capex and in seasonality, not receivables. Meghalaya officials reopened the historic Pinewood Banquet Hall to accommodate rising tourism numbers, which hit 18 lakh visitors last year [2]. **That is the demand signal for this city, and it is a banquet and MICE signal as much as a rooms signal.** Local coverage of the reopening is consistent across outlets [1][3], but none of it gives us occupancy, ARR or margin for Shillong properties, so collect from customer.

## What has changed now
**The only fresh local fact is supply-side: a restored heritage banquet venue is back in the market [1][2][3].** That adds event capacity and competition for existing banquet operators at the same time as it validates demand. Peer results are strong but they are national chains, not Shillong: ITC Hotels reported consolidated revenue from operations at Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, and EBITDA at Rs 337 crore, up 37 percent [4]; Ventive Hospitality reported 27 per cent revenue growth with EBITDA margin at 48 per cent in Q3 FY26 [5]; Leela's Q2 growth was driven by 30% RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led, with strong MICE demand [6]. **Read these as proof that pricing power exists in Indian hospitality, not as Shillong numbers.** The ICRA material is methodology and an old October 2024 rational report [8][9][10], so treat it as framework, not current local evidence.

## Where to grow
**Pursue owner-run hotels and banquet halls with an existing asset, a documented event book, and F&B attached.** The Pinewood reopening tells you the state is backing heritage and event tourism [2][3], so banquet-linked borrowers with a track record are the natural target. **Avoid standalone restaurants with no owned premises and greenfield resort capex into a seasonal hill market.** When a proposal lands, check the split between rooms, F&B and banquet revenue; if banquet is above half, ask for the forward booking register and the cancellation history.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against cash, not against the building.** Take monthly bank statements and GST returns, a quarterly stock-and-bookings statement, and a half-yearly unit-level P&L. **Size the limit to the low season, not the peak.** If the borrower cannot show a low-season debt-service cover, ask for a promoter guarantee and a pledge of the banquet booking receipts.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch banquet cancellations, average room rate slippage and any diversion of event advances into other businesses.** If monthly collections fall below the prior year for two consecutive months, ask for the booking register and a revised cash-flow. If the borrower cannot produce GST returns on time, stop fresh disbursement.
